title: Hytale Adaptive Surface: persistent geometry with selected-block materials
summary: Adaptive Surface 0.9.4 uses native persistent shape/material states behind one creative item. Helper items are hidden from search by ItemQuality.HideFromSearch. Baked and learned HD textures are selected into a single per-world pack and published after Hytale exits; clicked-block material is retained.
problem_class: adaptive block geometry and selective material texture loading
problem_description: One smoothing block must form slopes/corners, retain its shape/material across world saves, and copy the exact block a player right-clicked without rebuilding a large client atlas during play or preventing world startup.
context: User-confirmed 0.9.4 on Hytale 0.6.8. Initial 0.9.3 creative search exposed internal helpers and new donor material Rock_Calcite_Brick was absent from the active pack. Runtime pack replacement was blocked by the Windows ZIP lock. 0.9.4 corrected both and retains clicked-target behavior.
inputs: native cube textures and material variants
constraints: client assets must be registered before join
no runtime asset registrations during placement
one visible creative item and no command
new learned textures become available after restart
known_attempts: full HD catalogue active at startup
placement interaction sync data for clicked material

changes: Assign stable state IDs for material, orientation and topology
Keep the source item linked to every state
Refresh local topology after placement or break events
advantages: Persistent shapes without separate block entities
One creative item
Native save and item behavior
disadvantages: Original material and UV atlas strategy required further work
test_results: Earlier server fixture loaded 448 legacy states
Saved states were checked across restart
Client visual validation remained separate

solution_versions.description: 0.9.3 keeps the full baked catalogue dormant in the JAR and builds a small active pack from each saved world. It enables the pack in save config, keeps fallback UVs native, and selects the clicked material from placement interaction data.
changes: Scan saved chunk palettes and write ZAS_ActivePack.zip before world startup
Enable ZytaleGenerated:AdaptiveSurfaceWorld explicitly
Move 0.9.1 fallback states onto native atlas and model geometry
Use matching interaction destination plus clicked target or block face to select the material
Retain material while local topology changes shape
Use current-view raycast only when no client interaction context exists
advantages: World loads with 56 active appearances in observed save
No texture rebuild or asset registration on placement
Existing saved block IDs remain valid
Unknown materials can be prepared for a future restart
User reported result near-perfect after 0.9.3
disadvantages: A material first encountered during play may use stone until a later restart
Budget of 10 million HD pixels per world is a project guard, not a proven engine limit
Final click behavior lacks automated client trace
Full dedicated-server test was limited by native QUIC and shutdown errors

solution_versions.description: Adaptive Surface 0.9.4 keeps one searchable item, loads selected baked and newly learned HD materials through one enabled per-world ZIP, and publishes staged changes only after the Hytale server exits on Windows.
changes: Mark material helper items with custom ItemQuality ZAS_Internal (HideFromSearch=true) and Variant=true; preserve state IDs and leave the main Adaptive Surface item searchable.
Persist material requests, merge baked P and learned Q entries into the selected world pack, and disable the obsolete separate learned pack.
Prepare next-start.zip outside active asset paths during play; launch a small bundled javaw companion at shutdown to atomically replace the ZIP after server exit releases its file lock.
Cancel placement and notify the player when the clicked block has a copyable material that is not yet preloaded, rather than saving a stone fallback.
Keep selected-block interaction resolution and topology/material persistence from 0.9.3.
advantages: User confirmed creative inventory and new-material issues resolved in the installed 0.9.4 release
No live atlas rebuild or runtime asset registration
One active world pack; helper items excluded from ordinary creative search
Future material requests survive to later starts
disadvantages: New material first encountered while playing still requires leaving and reopening the world
Forced termination can delay pack publication; persisted requests allow recovery
Final client behavior was user-reported, not captured by instrumented client tests
test_results: Offline Gradle build and 12,137 assertions passed; asset and shared-atlas validators passed
Installed user save: 63 active HD materials and 5,308,416 texture pixels; Rock_Calcite_Brick present; 63 helpers use hidden quality
Three isolated full QUICHE server boots/shutdowns exited 0: 63, 64, then 65 active appearances; native asset check found exactly one main item and hidden helpers
External cube fixture learned a Q token and loaded its texture from the same active world ZIP on the next start; publisher output hash matched staged ZIP
User confirmed both reported issues resolved after testing the installed release

metrics.reliability: User-confirmed visual result plus three successful isolated full-server startup/shutdown cycles
metrics.performance: 63 active HD materials, 5,308,416 texture pixels in installed save

solution_versions.description: Adaptive Surface 0.10.0: bounded quad carriers, inverted corner and stacked-pair topology, donor-native transition profiles and offline atlas migration; includes 0.9.6 constructor-time single-JAR world-pack bootstrap.
changes: Choose an equivalent triangle basis whose whole carrier quad remains in the voxel, then pack native voxel-axis UVs in the existing 256x256 HD atlas
Add U1-U14 vertically mirrored solids and collision boxes; resolve undersides and stacked pairs from immutable terrain/anchors
Copy only native Group/TransitionTexture/TransitionToGroups/TransitionToTag; split identical-image aliases when native transition profiles differ
Retain old P/Q IDs and remap old Q atlases before asset loading; preserve previous model paths for fallback archives
Prepare and enable per-world asset pack in plugin constructor before AssetModule setup; no external publisher or installer required
advantages: Single distributable JAR
No runtime asset registration
Bounded geometry and unchanged per-material atlas capacity
Existing selected material IDs preserved
disadvantages: Visual acceptance of custom-model native blending and tint remains pending in client
Compact cached images cannot regain missing detail
Native APIs and renderer behavior require revalidation on game updates

solution_versions.description: Adaptive Surface 0.10.2: retain approved stacked M/U corner pairs while removing the withdrawn solid-ceiling underside adaptation. Restore 0.10.0 assets and keep saved material IDs stable.
changes: Only an Adaptive Surface anchor directly above enables underside inversion; a solid block above by itself does not.
Withdraw the uninstalled 0.10.1 pyramid candidate and restore the released 0.10.0 atlas, models, textures, hitboxes and helper IDs byte-for-byte.
Existing hanging states change through the normal local place/break refresh without changing the selected material; approved stacked pairs retain their M/U forms.
advantages: Matches the user's final scope: second and third reference shapes retained, first reference adaptation removed
No asset-layout migration or increase in atlas size
Existing saved IDs remain loadable
disadvantages: Previously placed hanging shapes require a local refresh to change; no player-world-wide chunk rewrite was performed
Final client visual check remains with the user
test_results: Gradle check/build passed 258187 assertions, including 1024 neighbourhood/anchor ceiling regressions
